title: Largest Color Value in a Directed Graph
summary: Given a directed graph with n nodes and m edges, where nodes are numbered from 0 to n-1, and each node has a color represented by a lowercase English letter, determine the largest color value of any valid path.
statement: Given a directed graph with n nodes and m edges, where nodes are numbered from 0 to n-1, and each node has a color represented by a lowercase English letter, determine the largest color value of any valid path. A valid path is a sequence of nodes connected by directed edges. The color value of a path is the count of nodes with the most frequently occurring color along the path. If the graph contains a cycle, return -1.
constraints: Node i has colors[i]; a path follows directed edges and its color value is its most frequent color count.
Return the largest path color value, or -1 if any directed cycle exists.
hints: A cycle invalidates the graph; topological processing detects one when fewer than n nodes are removed.
For every node keep the best count of each of 26 colors along a path ending there.
Propagate all color counts across outgoing edges, adding the destination color when it is processed.
Topological order ensures all predecessors contribute before a node leaves the queue, so the DP represents every path; an unprocessed node proves a cycle.
